svg.text: poke-singles-former: predict the opponent, then choose
src/pcsa/rl_training/former.py · 1,798,048 parameters · d 128 · 4 layers · 4 heads · shapes per decision (training batches add [G games, T decisions] in front)
row order: 0 our active · 1–2 our bench · 3–5 empty
6 their active · 7–11 their seen, then preview-only
matchup 6 speed order, their hit on us
stat low 6 · stat high 6 · could Mega
per side ×9: moved / switched / no action, Mega,
moved first, damage taken, faints, item/ability shown
turn/30, first turn · ids: our move, our switch-in,
0–3 move · 4–7 move + Mega · 8–10 switch to bench
memory: one field token per earlier decision
training computes every decision of a game in one pass
([T·14] sequence + a mask = the same concatenation)
Attention at each layer = a concatenation
out [14, 128] → next layer; this decision's field token at this
layer is stored and becomes memory for later decisions.
Each layer keeps its own memory list (≤ 64 field tokens).
Earlier decisions' other tokens (ours, theirs, last) are not
in memory: the field token carries each past turn forward.
live and training give identical outputs
~8 ms per decision on CPU (1 thread)
keep: revealed moves, then top by p (4) + 5 switches
logits_i = Σ_j p_kept_j · M[i, j] / τ
M[i, j] = 'how good my i is if they do j':
